tools.name: bull_create_rfq
tools.description: Use when you want to BUY a token in size (a block trade) without moving the market price: posts a private request for quotes on Bull, a non-custodial atomic OTC settlement layer. Returns an rfqId; sellers answer with sealed quotes only you can read. Optional maxPrice limit and webhook; set dryRun to

tools.name: bull_list_rfqs
tools.description: Use when you SELL or hold a token and want to find buyers: lists open requests for quotes on Bull (token, size in USD, window, buyer's price limit). Returns rfqIds to answer with bull_send_quote. Public, no signature needed. Not for finding market prices.

tools.name: bull_send_quote
tools.description: Use when you want to SELL tokens to a buyer who posted an RFQ: sends a sealed quote (token amount and total ETH price) that only the buyer sees. Returns a quoteId. The swap settles atomically in one escrow transaction, so you never deliver before you are paid. Not for listing prices publicly. Signed

tools.name: bull_get_quotes
tools.description: Use as a BUYER to read the sealed quotes on your own RFQ: seller, token amount, total price, counter state, deal status. Returns a list of quotes with quoteIds. Only the RFQ's buyer can read it. Signed: the first call returns a message to sign; call again with the same arguments plus timestamp and s

tools.name: bull_counter_quote
tools.description: Use as a BUYER to negotiate: propose a different total price (and optionally a different token amount) on a pending quote. Returns the stored counter. The seller can answer with bull_revise_quote. Works only while the quote is pending. Signed: the first call returns a message to sign; call again wit

tools.name: bull_revise_quote
tools.description: Use as a SELLER to change the price and/or token amount of your own pending quote, for example to meet the buyer's counter. Returns the new terms. The buyer then accepts with bull_accept_quote. Works only while the quote is pending. Signed: the first call returns a message to sign; call again with t

tools.name: bull_accept_quote
tools.description: Use as a BUYER to accept a quote. Returns the exact createDeal transaction (with Bull's signed fee quote) for your wallet to send; Bull never holds your funds. Then call bull_attach_deal with the dealId from the DealCreated event. Safe to call again to refresh the fee quote. Signed: the first call r

tools.name: bull_attach_deal
tools.description: Use as a BUYER after sending createDeal: report the dealId. Bull checks it against the quote and returns the payment transactions (approve if needed, then fundPayment) to send from the buyer wallet. When the seller deposits, the swap settles in that transaction. Signed: the first call returns a mess

tools.name: bull_deposit_plan
tools.description: Use as a SELLER after the buyer has paid into escrow: returns what to sign to deposit your tokens, either a gasless EIP-2612 permit (Bull's relayer pays gas) or direct approve + fundTokens transactions. Fails with not_ready until the buyer has funded. Signed: the first call returns a message to sign

tools.name: bull_deposit
tools.description: Use as a SELLER to submit the signed permit from bull_deposit_plan. Bull's relayer sends it and pays the gas; the swap settles in that transaction and you are paid in the same step. Returns the transaction hash. Signed: the first call returns a message to sign; call again with the same arguments plu

tools.name: bull_quote_status
tools.description: Use as BUYER or SELLER to check a quote and its onchain deal: status (pending, confirmed, funded, released), dealId, counter, who has funded. Poll this or use webhooks. Only the two parties can read it. Signed: the first call returns a message to sign; call again with the same arguments plus timesta

tools.name: bull_reject_quote
tools.description: Use as a BUYER to reject a quote you do not want. Returns status rejected. Not needed for quotes that simply expire. Signed: the first call returns a message to sign; call again with the same arguments plus timestamp and signature.

tools.name: bull_get_deal
tools.description: Use to verify any escrow deal onchain: open, settled or cancelled, and whether buyer and seller have funded. Public, no signature needed. Returns the deal state read from the contract.

tools.name: bull_get_receipt
tools.description: Use to get proof of a completed trade: a signed receipt for a settled deal (buyer, seller, token, amounts, fee) that anyone can re-check onchain. Public. Fails with not_settled for deals that are still open.

tools.name: bull_stats
tools.description: Use to check Bull's track record: number of settled deals, total volume, open RFQs and the latest settled deals, read from the escrow contract. Public, no signature needed.

tools.name: bull_info
tools.description: Use first to see what Bull is: supported chains, escrow contract, fee tiers, minimum size and auth rules. Public. Bull is a non-custodial atomic OTC/RFQ settlement layer.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: bull_create_rfq, bull_get_quotes, bull_quote_status · Private data: bull_create_rfq, bull_list_rfqs, bull_send_quote, bull_get_quotes, bull_counter_quote, bull_revise_quote, bull_accept_quote, bull_attach_deal, bull_deposit_plan, bull_get_receipt, bull_stats · Public sink: bull_create_rfq, bull_send_quote, bull_accept_quote, bull_attach_deal, bull_deposit.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: bull_create_rfq, bull_get_quotes, bull_quote_status · Private data: bull_create_rfq, bull_list_rfqs, bull_send_quote, bull_get_quotes, bull_counter_quote, bull_revise_quote, bull_accept_quote, bull_attach_deal, bull_deposit_plan, bull_get_receipt, bull_stats · Public sink: bull_create_rfq, bull_send_quote, bull_accept_quote, bull_attach_deal, bull_deposit

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
